quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that is a thick, warm forest that gets rain almost every single day!
quests.question: Rainforest
quests.hint: More different kinds of plants and animals live here than almost anywhere else on Earth.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Rainforest is correct because it is a thick, warm forest that gets rain almost every day.
quests.funFact: The Amazon Rainforest makes so much oxygen that people call it one of the 'lungs' of our planet!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that is a warm, dry grassland with scattered trees here and there!
quests.question: Savanna
quests.hint: This open, golden landscape has just enough trees to give occasional shade.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Savanna is correct because it is a warm, dry grassland with scattered trees.
quests.funFact: Savannas have two very different seasons each year: one very wet, and one very dry!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that is a cold, flat land where almost no trees can grow!
quests.question: Tundra
quests.hint: Frozen ground just beneath the surface keeps tall tree roots from ever growing deep.
quests.explanation: Yes! Tundra is correct because it is a cold, flat land where almost no trees can grow.
quests.funFact: The ground beneath the tundra stays frozen solid all year, even in the short summer!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that is a region of hills and mountains, higher than the land around it!
quests.question: Highlands
quests.hint: The air feels cooler and thinner as you travel up into this elevated region.
quests.explanation: Yes! Highlands is correct because it is a region of hills and mountains higher than the surrounding land.
quests.funFact: Some highland regions stay so cool that snow can fall even in the middle of summer!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that is flat land lying close to sea level!
quests.question: Lowlands
quests.hint: Rivers here flow gently, without the steep, rushing drops found in the mountains.
quests.explanation: Yes! Lowlands is correct because it is flat land lying close to sea level.
quests.funFact: Many of the world's biggest cities were built on lowlands because the flat ground is easy to build on!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that is the icy, frozen region surrounding the North Pole!
quests.question: Arctic
quests.hint: Thick sea ice covers much of the ocean in this freezing, faraway region.
quests.explanation: Yes! The Arctic is correct because it is the icy, frozen region surrounding the North Pole.
quests.funFact: The Arctic gets almost twenty-four hours of daylight during its short summer!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that stays warm and humid all year long, near the middle of the Earth!
quests.question: Tropics
quests.hint: This warm region almost never sees frost, snow, or a truly cold day.
quests.explanation: Yes! Tropics is correct because it stays warm and humid all year long, near the middle of the Earth.
quests.funFact: The tropics get the most direct sunlight of anywhere on Earth, all year round!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is the imaginary line circling the exact middle of the Earth!
quests.question: Equator
quests.hint: Places near this invisible line usually feel warm all year, with very little change in temperature.
quests.explanation: Yes! The Equator is correct because it is the imaginary line circling the exact middle of the Earth.
quests.funFact: Countries sitting right along the equator barely notice much difference between their seasons!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a large natural area with its own climate, plants, and animals!
quests.question: Biome
quests.hint: A rainforest, a desert, and a tundra are each a very different example of this.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Biome is correct because it is a large natural area with its own climate, plants, and animals.
quests.funFact: Scientists divide the whole Earth into several major biomes, each shaped by its own climate!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is the long, winding edge where land meets the sea!
quests.question: Coastline
quests.hint: This edge can be sandy and smooth, or rocky and jagged, depending on where you look.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Coastline is correct because it is the long, winding edge where land meets the sea.
quests.funFact: If you measured every twist and turn, a coastline can be far longer than a straight line on a map suggests!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place with layers of tall trees dripping with humidity and greenery!
quests.question: Rainforest
quests.hint: This warm, wet forest stays green and lush all year round, without any dry season.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Rainforest is correct because it has layers of tall trees dripping with humidity and greenery.
quests.funFact: A single rainforest tree can be home to hundreds of different kinds of insects!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place where tall golden grass stretches out beneath a few scattered trees!
quests.question: Savanna
quests.hint: This wide open land is much warmer and drier than a cool, temperate meadow.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Savanna is correct because tall golden grass stretches beneath its few scattered trees.
quests.funFact: Some of the largest savannas in the world are found across parts of Africa!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place covered in short, hardy plants instead of tall trees or forests!
quests.question: Tundra
quests.hint: Only small mosses, grasses, and tiny flowers can survive this icy, windswept land.
quests.explanation: That's right! Tundra is correct because it is covered in short, hardy plants instead of tall trees.
quests.funFact: During its brief summer, the tundra can suddenly burst into bloom with tiny colorful flowers!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place with rolling hills and rugged land that rises high above sea level!
quests.question: Highlands
quests.hint: Farmers here often raise hardy animals that can handle the steep, rocky ground.
quests.explanation: That's right! Highlands is correct because it has rolling hills and rugged land high above sea level.
quests.funFact: The Scottish Highlands are famous around the world for their misty hills and dramatic scenery!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place with rich, flat soil that's perfect for growing crops!
quests.question: Lowlands
quests.hint: Farmers love this gentle, low-lying land because it's so much easier to plow than a hillside.
quests.explanation: That's right! Lowlands is correct because its rich, flat soil is perfect for growing crops.
quests.funFact: Some lowlands sit so close to sea level that they need walls to help keep flood water out!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place where the ocean itself can freeze solid for months at a time!
quests.question: Arctic
quests.hint: This freezing region stays covered in ice and snow for most of the year.
quests.explanation: That's right! The Arctic is correct because its ocean can freeze solid for months at a time.
quests.funFact: Unlike the icy continent near the South Pole, the Arctic is mostly frozen ocean, not solid land!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place where rainforests and warm beaches are both common sights!
quests.question: Tropics
quests.hint: This region rarely has more than a wet season and a dry season, instead of four seasons.
quests.explanation: That's right! Tropics is correct because rainforests and warm beaches are both common there.
quests.funFact: Bananas, mangoes, and many other juicy fruits grow best in the warm, sunny tropics!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that divides the Earth into a northern half and a southern half!
quests.question: Equator
quests.hint: This invisible line splits our whole planet exactly down the middle.
quests.explanation: That's right! The Equator is correct because it divides the Earth into a northern half and a southern half.
quests.funFact: Sunlight hits the equator most directly, which is why places near it tend to be so warm!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object used to describe a big region like a desert, forest, or grassland together!
quests.question: Biome
quests.hint: Every one of these large natural regions has plants and animals specially suited to live there.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Biome is correct because it describes a big natural region like a desert, forest, or grassland.
quests.funFact: The same kind of biome, like a desert, can be found on many different continents around the world!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that stretches for miles, sometimes sandy and sometimes rocky!
quests.question: Coastline
quests.hint: Waves are constantly reshaping this long edge between the land and the sea.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Coastline is correct because it stretches for miles, sometimes sandy and sometimes rocky.
quests.funFact: Some countries have incredibly long coastlines simply because their land has so many bays and inlets!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place found near the equator where it's warm, wet, and incredibly green!
quests.question: Rainforest
quests.hint: This lush, crowded forest holds more living things packed together than any other place on land.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Rainforest is correct because it is the warm, wet, incredibly green place found near the equator.
quests.funFact: Even though rainforests cover a small part of the Earth, they hold more than half of all known plant and animal species!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place with wide open grassland that turns brown and dry for part of the year!
quests.question: Savanna
quests.hint: This warm grassland depends on a rainy season to keep its grass green and growing.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Savanna is correct because its open grassland turns brown and dry for part of the year.
quests.funFact: Savanna grass has extra-deep roots that help it survive the long, dry season!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place found near the North Pole where winters are long, dark, and freezing!
quests.question: Tundra
quests.hint: This treeless land stays frozen for most of the year, with only a short, cool summer.
quests.explanation: Great job! Tundra is correct because it is the freezing, treeless land found near the North Pole.
quests.funFact: Even though it's freezing most of the year, the tundra is home to surprisingly tough wildlife!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that stays noticeably cooler than the flatter land down below it!
quests.question: Highlands
quests.hint: Thick fog and mist often roll across this elevated, hilly region.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Highlands is correct because it stays noticeably cooler than the flatter land below.
quests.funFact: Many highland regions get much more rain than the lower, flatter land nearby!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that sits much closer to sea level than the hills and mountains nearby!
quests.question: Lowlands
quests.hint: Rivers slow down and spread out once they finally reach this flat, low-lying land.
quests.explanation: Great job! Lowlands is correct because it sits much closer to sea level than nearby hills and mountains.
quests.funFact: The Netherlands is famous for having so much of its lowland actually below sea level!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place known for its long, dark winters and icy, frozen landscape!
quests.question: Arctic
quests.hint: The Sun barely rises above the horizon here during the coldest, darkest months.
quests.explanation: Great choice! The Arctic is correct because it is known for its long, dark winters and icy landscape.
quests.funFact: The Arctic is warming faster than almost any other place on our entire planet!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place found closest to the invisible line running around Earth's middle!
quests.question: Tropics
quests.hint: This warm band circling the globe barely ever experiences a cold winter.
quests.explanation: Great job! Tropics is correct because it is found closest to the invisible line around Earth's middle.
quests.funFact: Even the coldest month in the tropics still usually feels warm compared to other parts of the world!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that stays the same distance from both the North Pole and the South Pole!
quests.question: Equator
quests.hint: This exact middle line wraps all the way around our entire planet.
quests.explanation: Great choice! The Equator is correct because it stays the same distance from both the North and South Poles.
quests.funFact: Days and nights near the equator stay almost exactly the same length all year round!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that groups together all the plants, animals, and weather of one big natural area!
quests.question: Biome
quests.hint: This word helps scientists compare very different natural places all around the world.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Biome is correct because it groups together the plants, animals, and weather of one big area.
quests.funFact: There are biomes found on land, and there are entirely different biomes found underwater!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that slowly changes shape as waves and tides shift the sand and rock!
quests.question: Coastline
quests.hint: This border between land and sea never looks exactly the same from year to year.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Coastline is correct because it slowly changes shape as waves and tides shift the sand and rock.
quests.funFact: Storms can dramatically reshape a sandy coastline in just a single night!
